02 .  This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the State.
Learned counsel for the State submits that notice on the respondent no.2 (informant) has been made sufficient on 26.05.2023.
None appears for the respondent no.2.

This is an appeal under section 14-A(2) of S.C. & S.T. (PoA)
Act, 1989 in connection with C.T. Case No.59 of 2023 arising out of Badambadi P.S. Case No.81 of 2023 pending in the Spl. Court under SC & // 2 // ST (PoA) Act, Cuttack for offences punishable under sections 341/323/294/420/498-A/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code read with section 3(1)(r)/3(2)(va) of SC & ST (PoA) Act.

The appellant moved an application for bail before the learned Spl. Court under SC & ST (PoA) Act,
Cuttack, which was rejected on 13.04.2023.

sentences.text:
Let the appellant be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.50,000/-
(rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin over the matter with further conditions as the learned Court may deem just and proper with further conditions that he shall not indulge in any criminal activities and shall // 3 // appear before the learned trial Court on each date to which the case would be posted for trial.

opennyai_summary.decision:
The appellant moved an application for bail before the learned Spl. Court under SC & ST (PoA) Act,
Cuttack, which was rejected on 13.04.2023.
Considering the submission made by the learned counsel for the appellant that the respondent no.2 is the wife of the appellant and on account of matrimonial dispute between the parties, the case has been instituted and divorce proceeding is also subjudiced in the Court of learned Judge, Family Court, Cuttack and the appellant is in judicial custody since 13.04.2023 and after hearing learned counsel for the State and going through the documents annexed to appeal memo, I am inclined to release the appellant on bail.
Let the appellant be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.50,000/-
(rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin over the matter with further conditions as the learned Court may deem just and proper with further conditions that he shall not indulge in any criminal activities and shall // 3 // appear before the learned trial Court on each date to which the case would be posted for trial.
Violation of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
The CRLA is accordingly disposed of.
